item.title: NSF ERI award for multi-fidelity modeling of heterogeneous materials
item.description:
The National Science Foundation has made an Engineering Research Initiation award of $200,000 over two years, for an Adaptive Multi-Fidelity Framework for Modeling Heterogeneous Materials Under Extreme Conditions.

Resolving deformation and fracture inside every grain of a granular assembly is expensive, and many regions may not require particle-scale resolution at every stage of loading. The project is about deciding where the expensive description is needed and where a cheaper one will do, while estimating the error introduced by the coarser description. Progress is on the granular mechanics project page.

item.title: SDBOR Competitive Research Grant awarded for modeling and design of magnetic soft materials
item.description:
The South Dakota Board of Regents has awarded a $90,000 Competitive Research Grant for Modeling and Design of Magnetic Soft Materials Accelerated by Neural Operators, running from June 2025 through April 2027. It is the second award announced this week, alongside the NSF ERI award.

The work has three parts. The first is to compare the available models of effective material properties in magnetic soft composites, and establish which of them can be relied on for design rather than description. The second is to build topology optimization solvers that treat structural density and magnetization as one coupled problem. The third is to use neural operator surrogates to make the repeated forward solves that optimization requires affordable. This connects the material-design problem with the group’s work on residual-based error estimation and correction for neural operators.

item.title: Virtual Thematic Conference (January 10 - 11, 2022) on Computational Oncology
item.description:
With Ernesto Lima and Chengyue Wu at the Oden Institute, I organized a virtual thematic conference on computational oncology, held January 10-11, 2022 with the support of the Biological Systems TTA in USACM. The meeting brought together researchers across computational oncology to discuss modeling, data, and validation questions in computational oncology.

The archived meeting page carries the program and speaker information. The conference flyer appears below, and is also available as a PDF.
